<div id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Partial Attention (PA).</span>
PA focuses on limiting the scope of attention to a subset of tokens, thereby reducing computational demands. The Swin Transformer<span id="footnote4" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">4</span>
                
                
                
              <a href="https://github.com/microsoft/Swin-Transformer" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/microsoft/Swin-Transformer</a></span></span></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib111" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2021</a>)</cite> achieves this by using shifted windows to confine self-attention computations to non-overlapping local windows, resulting in linear computational growth. Specifically, assuming each window contains <math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times M</annotation></semantics></math> pixels, the computational complexities of the standard global Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) module and   the Window-based Multi-head Self-Attention (WMSA) on the input image with <math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\times w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\times w</annotation></semantics></math> patches are as follows:</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E2X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_left">(2)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E2X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\Omega(\mathrm{MSA})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>MSA</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\Omega(\mathrm{MSA})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E2X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=4hw\mathrm{C}^{2}+2(hw)^{2}\mathrm{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=4hw\mathrm{C}^{2}+2(hw)^{2}\mathrm{C}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.E2Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E2Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\Omega(\mathrm{W}\mathrm{MSA})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>WMSA</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\Omega(\mathrm{W}\mathrm{MSA})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E2Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=4hw\mathrm{C}^{2}+2M^{2}hw\mathrm{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=4hw\mathrm{C}^{2}+2M^{2}hw\mathrm{C}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where the <math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{C}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the embedding dimension, symbol <math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega</annotation></semantics></math> is used to measure the computation complexity, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega(\mathrm{MHSA})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>MHSA</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega(\mathrm{MHSA})</annotation></semantics></math> has a quadratic complexity with respect to the number of patches <math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\times w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\times w</annotation></semantics></math>, while the <math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega(\mathrm{W}\mathrm{MSA})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>WMSA</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega(\mathrm{W}\mathrm{MSA})</annotation></semantics></math> has a promising linear complexity.
Similarly, the CSWin Transformer <span id="footnote5" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">5</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">5</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">5</span>
                
                
                
              <a href="https://github.com/microsoft/CSWin-Transformer" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/microsoft/CSWin-Transformer</a></span></span></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib102" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dong et al., 2022</a>)</cite> partitions the input features into horizontal and vertical stripes and computes SA within these localized regions, as shown in Figure <a href="#S3.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 3.3.1. Self-Attention ‣ 3.3. Efficient Token Update ‣ 3. Efficient ViT Components ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.
The TNT <span id="footnote6" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">6</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">6</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">6</span>
                
                
                
              <a href="https://github.com/lucidrains/transformer-in-transformer" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/lucidrains/transformer-in-transformer</a></span></span></span> model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib112" title="" class="ltx_ref">Han et al., 2021</a>)</cite> employs transformers at the patch and pixel levels, facilitating detailed attention to local features.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Local Self-Attention.</span>
Local SA takes the idea of partial attention by restricting attention operations to local regions of the input image <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib113" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
Multi-axis attention (Max-SA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib105" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tu et al., 2022</a>)</cite> simplifies the complexity of attention from quadratic to linear by implementing windowed and mesh attention, while ReViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib109" title="" class="ltx_ref">Diko et al., 2024</a>)</cite> addresses feature collapse in deep ViT layers through residual attention learning. Deformable self-attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib114" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xia et al., 2022</a>)</cite> and dynamic sparse attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib108" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib115" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tamura, 2024</a>)</cite> dynamically select attention blocks based on data dependencies and query patterns, respectively. The Focal Self-attention model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib104" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2021</a>)</cite> captures both short-range and long-range dependencies, utilizing fine-grained local attention and coarse-grained distant interactions. ViL<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib116" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2021</a>)</cite> combines multi-scale architectures with extended context considerations, improving high-resolution image processing and encoding.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2505.03113v3/MLP.png" id="S3.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/98;" width="476" height="98" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6. </span>
<span id="S3.F6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Attention-Free Paradigm for Token Updates.</span>
MLP-Mixer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib117" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tolstikhin et al., 2021</a>)</cite> proposes to replace convolution and attention in ViT with MLP models. The figure shows the key part of the MLP-Mixer, which contains mixing patches and mixing channels.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Linear Self-Attention.</span>
Linear SA aims to reduce the computational complexity of SA from quadratic to linear <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib118" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lu et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.
Various methods are proposed, such as replacing dot product attention with position-sensitive hashing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib119" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kitaev et al., 2020</a>)</cite>.
GFNet <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib103" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rao et al., 2021</a>)</cite> employs discrete two-dimensional Fourier transforms combined with a learnable global filter, and Linformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib120" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2020</a>)</cite> introduces a low-rank matrix to achieve linear complexity.
SwiftFormer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib107" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shaker et al., 2023</a>)</cite> uses an efficient additive attention mechanism, while <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib121" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mehta and Rastegari, 2022</a>)</cite> proposes separable self-attention using element-wise intelligent operations. The neighborhood attention mechanism <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib122" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2023</a>)</cite> adjusts attention weights based on the 2D Manhattan distance from neighboring patches.
Similarly, Vision Outlooker (VOLO) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib123" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yuan et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, while primarily focusing on computer vision tasks, introduces an innovative locality-sensitive attention mechanism, balancing efficiency and accuracy.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Low-Rank Decomposition.</span>
These techniques decompose the attention matrix into low-dimensional representations to optimize the computation. MobileViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib124" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mehta and Rastegari, 2021</a>)</cite> combines low-rank decomposition and sparsification techniques to transform ViT into a mobile-friendly version. The Low-Rank Transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib125" title="" class="ltx_ref">Katharopoulos et al., 2020</a>)</cite> reduces computational complexity by decomposing the SA layer, while the Performer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib126" title="" class="ltx_ref">Choromanski et al., 2020</a>)</cite> integrates kernel techniques with low-rank decomposition.
Tensor decomposition techniques, such as CP-Decomposition <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib127" title="" class="ltx_ref">Novikov et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib128" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lebedev et al., 2014</a>)</cite>, and factorized self-attention mechanisms <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib129" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2021</a>)</cite> have also been applied for model optimization.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.3.2. </span><span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Attention-Free Architecture</span></h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While self-attention revolutionizes the field of image recognition, its computational complexity motivates the exploration of alternative architectures that achieve comparable performance with reduced resource requirements and leads to renewed interest in MLP, a classic neural network architecture consisting of fully connected layers and activation functions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">MLP-based architectures, often dispensing with the complexities of convolutional and self-attention mechanisms, offer advantages in terms of adaptability and computational efficiency.
This topic focuses on two main directions in MLP research for efficient image recognition: <span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pure MLP Architecture</span> and <span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Hybrid MLP-CNN Architecture</span>.
These approaches highlight the potential of the MLP design as a competitive alternative to attention-based models.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pure MLP Architecture.</span>
Pure MLP architectures aim to simplify the token update operation for improved efficiency while maintaining performance.
ResMLP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib130" title="" class="ltx_ref">Touvron et al., 2021</a>)</cite> introduces a residual network architecture that alternates between linear layers and two-layer feedforward networks.
As shown in Figure <a href="#S3.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 3.3.1. Self-Attention ‣ 3.3. Efficient Token Update ‣ 3. Efficient ViT Components ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, MLP-Mixer<span id="footnote7" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">7</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">7</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">7</span>
                
                
                
              <a href="https://github.com/jaketae/mlp-mixer" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/jaketae/mlp-mixer</a></span></span></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib117" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tolstikhin et al., 2021</a>)</cite> introduces Token-Mixing and Channel-Mixing MLP blocks to process images, avoiding convolutions and SA.
S2-MLP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib131" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, inspired by MLP-Mixer, relies on channel mixing and incorporates a spatial shift operation for patch interaction.
AS-MLP<span id="footnote8" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">8</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">8</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">8</span>
                
                
                
              <a href="https://github.com/svip-lab/AS-MLP" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/svip-lab/AS-MLP</a></span></span></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib132" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lian et al., 2022</a>)</cite> adopts axially shifted channels to capture local dependencies, allowing the pure MLP model to simulate the local receptive fields of CNN models.
MLP-Unet <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib133" title="" class="ltx_ref">Saikia et al., 2023</a>)</cite> applies a fully MLP-based method and cascaded upsampler to keep local information effectively.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T4" class="ltx_table">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 4. </span>
A quantitative comparative analysis is conducted on the classic methods involved in <span id="S3.T4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Attention-Free Design</span> (Section <a href="#S3.SS3.SSS2" title="3.3.2. Attention-Free Architecture ‣ 3.3. Efficient Token Update ‣ 3. Efficient ViT Components ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3.2</span></a>), using ImageNet-1K as the benchmark, with the resolution standardized to <math id="S3.T4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="224\times 224" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>224</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>224</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">224\times 224</annotation></semantics></math>.
The “/16” in Mixer means the model of base scale with patches of resolution <math id="S3.T4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16\times 16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16\times 16</annotation></semantics></math>
The best-performing method is highlighted in bold, and the runner-up is underlined.
</figcaption><div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<div id="S3.T4.4" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:169.1pt;height:76.2pt;vertical-align:-37.3pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-185.2pt,83.5pt) scale(0.313382051169342,0.313382051169342) ;">
<table id="S3.T4.4.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_middle">

<span id="S3.T4.4.1.1.5.2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_right" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;">Top-1 Acc.</span></span>

</span></span><span id="S3.T4.4.1.1.5.2.2" class="ltx_text"></span></span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T4.4.1.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S3.T4.4.1.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.T4.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="11.07" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 11.07 11.07" width="11.07"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#808080;--ltx-fill-color:#808080;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;" color="#808080" fill="#808080" stroke="#808080" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,11.07) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 11.07 0 L 5.53 11.07 Z"></path></g></svg></span> GMLP-T <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib134" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2021</a>)</cite></td>
<td id="S3.T4.4.1.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;">2021</td>

<td id="S3.T4.5.1.16.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right" style="padding-top:1.95pt;padding-bottom:1.95pt;"><span id="S3.T4.5.1.16.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">6.3</span></td>

<tr id="S3.T4.5.1.17" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">

<tr id="S3.T4.5.1.19" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S3.T4.5.1.19.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:1.95pt;padding-bottom:1.95pt;"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.T4.pic36" class="ltx_picture" height="8.99" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 8.99 8.99" width="8.99"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#521CB7;--ltx-fill-color:#521CB7;--ltx-fg-color:#521CB7;" color="#521CB7" fill="#521CB7" stroke="#521CB7" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,8.99) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 M 0 0 L 0 8.99 L 8.99 8.99 L 8.99 0 Z M 8.99 8.99"></path></g></svg></span> MONet-S <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib142" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., 2024</a>)</cite></td>

<td id="S3.T4.5.1.19.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:1.95pt;padding-bottom:1.95pt;">81.3</td></tr>
</table>
</span></div></div></div>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Hybrid MLP-CNN Structure.</span>
Hybrid attention-free structures that integrate MLP and CNN offer a promising balance of complementary strengths.
X-MLP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib143" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2023a</a>)</cite> employs linear projections for feature map interactions, eliminating the need for convolution operations in patch embedding. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib144" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2023b</a>)</cite> propose a pre-training method that does not rely on attention mechanisms. gMLP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib134" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2021</a>)</cite> identifies the high computational burden of self-attention and uses channel and static spatial projections to maintain high precision with fewer parameters.
A hybrid model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib145" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ji et al., 2023</a>)</cite> achieves performance comparable to CNN-Transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib146" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cao et al., 2024</a>)</cite> hybrids by employing matrix decomposition and multiscale information fusion.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib147" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gu et al., 2022</a>)</cite> propose a structured state space method for efficiently modeling long sequences. US-MLP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib148" title="" class="ltx_ref">Luo et al., 2023</a>)</cite> integrates CNN layers with sparse MLP blocks.
Furthermore, GSS model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib149" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mehta et al., 2022</a>)</cite> effectively processes long sequence modeling through a gated state space, providing immense potential for image recognition applications. Similarly, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib147" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gu et al., 2022</a>)</cite> addresses the computational bottleneck in long sequence processing by optimizing state space modeling. PoolFormer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib140" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2022b</a>)</cite> <span id="footnote9" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">9</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">9</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">9</span>
                
                
                
              <a href="https://github.com/sail-sg/poolformer" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/sail-sg/poolformer</a> </span></span></span>replaces self-attention with grouping operations as a token mixer.
Finally, Mamba <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib150" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gu and Dao, 2024</a>)</cite> achieves linear time complexity in sequence modeling through selective state space. By applying a selective state space, Mamba effectively balances accuracy and computational burden in sequence modeling <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib151" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib152" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib153" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pei et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib154" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib155" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.3.3. </span><span id="S3.SS3.SSS3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Summary: Efficient Token Update</span></h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Self-Attention Optimization.</span>
While self-attention captures long-distance dependencies, its computational complexity increases with large datasets like ImageNet-1K. The goal is to optimize complexity without losing global dependency capture.
We report the relevant experimental results in Table  <a href="#S3.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 3.3.1. Self-Attention ‣ 3.3. Efficient Token Update ‣ 3. Efficient ViT Components ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, where it can be observed that:
<span id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">(i).</span> Methods based on local self-attention, such as GFNet <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib156" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rao et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and SKIPAT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib106" title="" class="ltx_ref">Venkataramanan et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, slightly compromise accuracy but significantly reduce computational burden. For example, SKIPAT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib106" title="" class="ltx_ref">Venkataramanan et al., 2023</a>)</cite> reduces the parameters to 5.8M and the FLOPs to <math id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.1</annotation></semantics></math>G;
<span id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">(ii).</span> BiFormer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib108" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu et al., 2023</a>)</cite> achieves an excellent balance between parameters, computational cost, and accuracy, with 13.1M parameters and only <math id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.2</annotation></semantics></math>G FLOPs, while attaining an accuracy of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="81.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>81.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">81.4\%</annotation></semantics></math>;
<span id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">(iii).</span> SSViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib110" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fan et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, as a state-of-the-art method, demonstrates an impressive accuracy of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="85.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>85.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">85.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> with only <math id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.1</annotation></semantics></math>G FLOPs, which is lower than the DeiT standard model, indicating that optimization of self-attention still holds potential.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T5" class="ltx_table">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 5. </span>

<td id="S3.T5.5.1.14.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;"><span id="S3.T5.5.1.14.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">40.0</span></td>
<td id="S3.T5.5.1.14.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;"><span id="S3.T5.5.1.14.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">86.1</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T5.5.1.15" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">
<td id="S3.T5.5.1.15.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.T5.pic33" class="ltx_picture" height="8.3" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 11.07 8.3" width="11.07"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#9962C0;--ltx-fill-color:#9962C0;--ltx-fg-color:#9962C0;" color="#9962C0" fill="#9962C0" stroke="#9962C0" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,8.3) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 M 0 0 L 0 8.3 L 11.07 8.3 L 11.07 0 Z M 11.07 8.3"></path></g></svg></span><span id="S3.T5.5.1.15.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;"> Hiera-H <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib163" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ryali et al., 2023</a>)</cite></span></td>
<td id="S3.T5.5.1.15.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;"><span id="S3.T5.5.1.15.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">2023</span></td>
<td id="S3.T5.5.1.15.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;"><span id="S3.T5.5.1.15.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">673.0</span></td>
<td id="S3.T5.5.1.15.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;"><span id="S3.T5.5.1.15.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">125.0</span></td>
<td id="S3.T5.5.1.15.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;"><span id="S3.T5.5.1.15.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">86.9</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T5.5.1.16" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S3.T5.5.1.16.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.T5.pic34" class="ltx_picture" height="8.99" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 8.99 8.99" width="8.99"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#E0BE9F;--ltx-fill-color:#E0BE9F;--ltx-fg-color:#E0BE9F;" color="#E0BE9F" fill="#E0BE9F" stroke="#E0BE9F" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,8.99) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 M 0 0 L 0 8.99 L 8.99 8.99 L 8.99 0 Z M 8.99 8.99"></path></g></svg></span> HIRI-ViT-S <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib164" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al., 2024</a>)</cite></td>

<td id="S3.T5.5.1.16.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;">4.5</td>
<td id="S3.T5.5.1.16.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;">83.6</td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T5.5.1.17" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S3.T5.5.1.17.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.T5.pic35" class="ltx_picture" height="8.99" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 8.99 8.99" width="8.99"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#E0BE9F;--ltx-fill-color:#E0BE9F;--ltx-fg-color:#E0BE9F;" color="#E0BE9F" fill="#E0BE9F" stroke="#E0BE9F" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,8.99) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 M 0 0 L 0 8.99 L 8.99 8.99 L 8.99 0 Z M 8.99 8.99"></path></g></svg></span> HIRI-ViT-B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib164" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al., 2024</a>)</cite></td>

<tr id="S3.T5.5.1.18" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S3.T5.5.1.18.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.T5.pic36" class="ltx_picture" height="8.99" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 8.99 8.99" width="8.99"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#E0BE9F;--ltx-fill-color:#E0BE9F;--ltx-fg-color:#E0BE9F;" color="#E0BE9F" fill="#E0BE9F" stroke="#E0BE9F" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,8.99) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 M 0 0 L 0 8.99 L 8.99 8.99 L 8.99 0 Z M 8.99 8.99"></path></g></svg></span> HIRI-ViT-L <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib164" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al., 2024</a>)</cite></td>

<td id="S3.T5.5.1.18.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;">17.0</td>
<td id="S3.T5.5.1.18.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:1.8pt;padding-bottom:1.8pt;">85.3</td></tr>
</table>
</span></div></div></div>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Attention-Free Design.</span>
The MLP design enhances computational efficiency by eliminating complex attention calculations, enabling faster adaptation to various hardware and optimization strategies.
When combined with CNNs, MLPs leverage their computational efficiency while keeping the exceptional feature extraction capabilities of CNNs, achieving a balance between performance and efficiency.
Table Y presents comparative results of relevant methods, revealing the following observations:
<span id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">(i).</span> HireMLP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib135" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2021</a>)</cite> series exhibit outstanding performance with relatively fewer parameters and lower FLOPs. For example, HireMLP-Small achieves an accuracy of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="82.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>82.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">82.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> using only 33M parameters and 4.2G FLOPs.
<span id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">(ii).</span> The hybrid MLP-CNN architecture can be adjusted according to specific requirements, accommodating various application scenarios and resource constraints. HireMLP-Small <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib135" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2021</a>)</cite> achieves an accuracy of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="82.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>82.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">82.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> with only <math id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.2</annotation></semantics></math> G FLOPs.
<span id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">(iii).</span> Particularly notable is SVT-H-L <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib122" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, which achieves an impressive Top-1 accuracy of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="85.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>85.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">85.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> using only 54M parameters and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12.7</annotation></semantics></math>G FLOPs.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4. </span><span id="S3.SS4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Framework Design</span></h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Inspired by hierarchical structures in convolutional neural networks for feature extraction and image pyramiding, researchers are integrating these principles into vision transformer (ViT) architectures. This hierarchical design aims to improve the efficiency of ViT and the learning of representation.
Hierarchical ViTs differentiate background and foreground objects, improving image recognition in complex scenes with varied scales or occlusions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib165" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.
This topic explores hierarchical ViT design, with the aim of capturing features at multiple scales for both global context and fine details.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Hierarchical Framework.</span>
Swin Transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib111" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2021</a>)</cite> leads the integration of hierarchical structure into ViT models, introducing shifted window attention and subsampling techniques.
PVT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib157" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2021</a>)</cite> and PVTv2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib97" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2022</a>)</cite> address these issues using a pyramid structure, linear complexity attention, and overlapping patch embeddings.
FDViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib160" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2023a</a>)</cite> introduces an innovative downsampling module to address the issue of excessive information loss caused by traditional integer-stride downsampling, and allows the reduction of feature map dimensions with non-integer strides, thereby smoothly decreasing computational complexity while preserving more information.
The Twins <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib159" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chu et al., 2021</a>)</cite> architecture introduces two hierarchical ViT variants: Twins-PCPVT and Twins-SVT. Twins-PCPVT improves the performance of PVT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib157" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2021</a>)</cite> through conditional positional encoding, and Twins-SVT employs a robust local-global decoupled SA mechanism, enabling exceptional local detail capture and global information processing.
MaxViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib105" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tu et al., 2022</a>)</cite> introduces multi-axis attention blocks (Max-SA) to blend local and global paradigms, maintaining efficacy at different resolutions.
H-MHSA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib166" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024</a>)</cite> further refines these approaches by maintaining granularity while modeling global and local dependencies. CvT<span id="footnote10" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">10</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">10</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">10</span>
              
              
              
            <a href="https://github.com/microsoft/CvT" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/microsoft/CvT</a></span></span></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib86" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2021</a>)</cite> takes a different route by integrating convolutions directly into the vision transformer architecture, using the hierarchical feature extraction capabilities of the CNN models to create a multi-stage structure. This approach bridges the gap between the CNN and ViT models, combining their strengths. Similarly, PiT<span id="footnote11" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">11</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">11</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">11</span>
              
              
              
            <a href="https://github.com/naver-ai/pit" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/naver-ai/pit</a></span></span></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib167" title="" class="ltx_ref">Heo et al., 2021</a>)</cite> proposes methods to better handle spatial dimensions, improving the hierarchical processing of spatial information.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Other Framework.</span>
For the efficiency exploration aspect of the novelty structure, Mask R-CNN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib168" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2021</a>)</cite> demonstrates how strategic partitioning can enhance task performance through various upsampling or downsampling operations. ViT-Adapter <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib169" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2023</a>)</cite> introduces a pre-training-free adapter for more effective inductive bias transfer. Using self-supervised techniques, MixMAE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib170" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023</a>)</cite> by using visible tokens from different images for reconstruction reduces computational demand.
HiViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib171" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2022</a>)</cite> improves efficiency by excluding all masked tokens. Complementary approaches, such as the asymmetric encoder-decoder structure <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib172" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, significantly reduce memory usage by clustering attention and sparse convolutions. Hiera <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib163" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ryali et al., 2023</a>)</cite> advances these ideas by removing non-transformer elements and enhancing image recognition analysis.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.4.1. </span><span id="S3.SS4.SSS1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Summary: Framework Design</span></h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Traditional ViTs generate single-resolution feature maps, limiting multi-scale information capture for image recognition.
By introducing a hierarchical structure design into the ViT architecture, it gains the ability to extract fine-grained features and effectively overcomes isotropy, enabling it to adapt to a diverse range of recognition tasks.
We provide relevant experimental results in Table <a href="#S3.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 3.3.3. Summary: Efficient Token Update ‣ 3.3. Efficient Token Update ‣ 3. Efficient ViT Components ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, where it can be observed that models utilizing hierarchical structures for multi-scale feature extraction generally exhibit superior performance in terms of accuracy.
In particular, the SOTA Hiera-H <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib163" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ryali et al., 2023</a>)</cite> not only possesses exceptional parameters and FLOPs, but also achieves the highest accuracy of <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>86.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86.9\%</annotation></semantics></math>.
HAT-Net and Hiera offer diverse optimizations in parameters and computational complexity compared to traditional ViTs and can be flexibly adapted to models of varying capacities to accommodate practical application requirements.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.5. </span><span id="S3.SS5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Efficient ViT Component Discussion</span></h3>

<div id="S3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we focus on the internal components of the vision transformer and the efforts made to achieve a balance between efficiency and precision. We present the methods in the order of the image input flow through the network, specifically highlighting four aspects of technical innovation: Embedding Structure Design, Efficient Position Encoding, Efficient Token Update, and Framework Design. In addition, we discuss the relevance of these components in the broader scope of image recognition, emphasizing how they contribute to the overall accuracy and speed of the model.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Tables <a href="#S3.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 3.1. Embedding Structure Design ‣ 3. Efficient ViT Components ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, <a href="#S3.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 3.3.1. Self-Attention ‣ 3.3. Efficient Token Update ‣ 3. Efficient ViT Components ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, <a href="#S3.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 3.3.2. Attention-Free Architecture ‣ 3.3. Efficient Token Update ‣ 3. Efficient ViT Components ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and <a href="#S3.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 3.3.3. Summary: Efficient Token Update ‣ 3.3. Efficient Token Update ‣ 3. Efficient ViT Components ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> present the precision benchmarks of these methods and its variants on the ImageNet dataset, highlighting the trade-offs achieved between performance and efficiency at a consistent resolution of <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="224\times 224" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>224</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>224</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">224\times 224</annotation></semantics></math>.
From these tables, several conclusions can be drawn:</p>
<ol id="S3.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">a.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Advancements in patch embedding and positional encoding, often implemented independently, flexibly integrate into existing frameworks, mitigating the need for extensive hyperparameter tuning and specialized optimization techniques;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">b.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Locality emerges as a driving force in enhancing ViT component performance. This is evident in patch embedding that focuses on local regions through the attention mechanism, the reduction of self-attention scope or integration of CNN models, and the hierarchical information extraction in framework design.
These strategies yield  significant efficiency gains without compromising performance;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">c.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While shifting from self-attention to attention-free designs demonstrably reduces FLOPs, recent self-attention optimization designs demonstrate a compelling balance between performance and efficiency.
Therefore, exploring optimization strategies targeting the complexity of self-attention remains a promising direction for future research;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">d.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The performance gains observed in hierarchical structures for dense prediction tasks are particularly noteworthy when compared to recognition tasks, suggesting that developing a general hierarchical architecture for multiple vision tasks is a research direction worthy of further exploration.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we follow the sequence in which the input stream is forwarded within the ViT models to present the methods involved, offering the advantage of:</p>
<ol id="S3.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S3.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">a.</span> 
<div id="S3.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">By analyzing the performance bottlenecks of existing models, we can determine which component corresponds to lightweight measures. This section facilitates this process by providing a straightforward and accessible comparative framework.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">b.</span> 
<div id="S3.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">By emphasizing the relative independence of ViT components, this offers a perspective on adaptive and integrated optimization, which allows the selection of multiple components along the input stream to achieve lightweight design.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2505.03113v3/n7.png" id="S3.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/210;" width="476" height="210" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7. </span>
<span id="S3.F7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic Resolution Exploration Timeline.</span>
The figure collects and organizes the development history of dynamic resolution methods in ViT model lightweighting. It is mainly divided into two parts: token pruning and token merging.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S3.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2505.03113v3/picture/n4.png" id="S3.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:452/85;" width="452" height="85" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8. </span>
<span id="S3.F8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Space Redundancy Solution Comparison.</span>
The CNN models typically employ a structural downsampling strategy, as illustrated in <math id="S3.F8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a)</annotation></semantics></math>. The unstructured and data-dependent downsampling method in <math id="S3.F8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(b)</annotation></semantics></math> more effectively capitalizes on the sparsity within the input data. Owing to the inherent characteristics of the self-attention operation, the unstructured token set is also accelerated through parallel computing.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S3.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2505.03113v3/token-pruning.png" id="S3.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:333/213;" width="333" height="213" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 9. </span>
<span id="S3.F9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Token Selection Example</span>.
Evo-ViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib173" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2021</a>)</cite> uses a token selector to pick informative tokens for slow updates and less-informative tokens for fast updates.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4. </span><span id="S4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic Network</span></h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Dynamic networks represent a critical evolution in the field of image recognition, dramatically improving precision by flexibly adapting their computational structures to the complexities of varying inputs. Unlike static models, which operate on fixed computational graphs and parameters, dynamic networks can tailor their internal configurations, thus achieving better computational efficiency and adaptability. This adaptability is particularly beneficial in image recognition tasks, where the complexity of images can vary widely.
Furthermore, the dynamic network paradigm is one of the specific forms of online lightweighting strategies, where the computational load is reduced dynamically to maintain efficiency without compromising accuracy. In this section, we categorize dynamic networks based on the vision transformer into two primary topics to review the rapid advances: <span id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic Resolution</span> in Section <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1. Dynamic Resolution ‣ 4. Dynamic Network ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> and <span id="S4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Depth Adaptation</span> in Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2. Depth Adaptation ‣ 4. Dynamic Network ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1. </span><span id="S4.SS1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic Resolution</span></h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Figure <a href="#S3.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 3.5. Efficient ViT Component Discussion ‣ 3. Efficient ViT Components ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, unlike traditional convolutional neural networks, which often employ coarse sampling methods when faced with spatial redundancy or the need for downsampling, ViT models possess the unique token representation advantage, allowing for more customized and fine-grained downsampling strategies.
Specifically, decisions are made about whether each token is pruned, kept, or merged based on its significance. This approach has proven particularly beneficial for image recognition tasks, where the ability to dynamically adjust the resolution and focus on significant regions of an image can greatly enhance the accuracy and efficiency of the model. From these applications, we summarize two main topics: <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic Token Pruning</span> and <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic Token Merging</span>.
In Figure <a href="#S3.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ 3.5. Efficient ViT Component Discussion ‣ 3. Efficient ViT Components ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, we summarize the timeline of significant explorations on these two topics.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2505.03113v3/picture/n6.png" id="S4.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/229;" width="476" height="229" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 10. </span>
<span id="S4.F10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Token Pruning Visualization</span>.
Visualize and compare different token pruning methods. Here, <math id="S4.F10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> represents the token keep rate, and the masked tokens are shown on a white background.
Generally, the higher the attention to the object, the more effective the token pruning method is considered.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S4.T6" class="ltx_table">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6. </span>
A quantitative comparative analysis is conducted on the classic methods involved in <span id="S4.T6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic Token Pruning</span> (Section <a href="#S4.SS1.SSS1" title="4.1.1. Dynamic Token Pruning ‣ 4.1. Dynamic Resolution ‣ 4. Dynamic Network ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1.1</span></a>), using ImageNet-1K as the benchmark, with the resolution standardized to <math id="S4.T6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="224\times 224" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>224</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>224</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">224\times 224</annotation></semantics></math>.
The R in “/R" indicates the ratio of token pruning.
The best-performing method is highlighted in bold, and the runner-up is underlined.
</figcaption><div class="ltx_flex_figure">

<figure id="S4.T7" class="ltx_table">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 7. </span>
A quantitative comparative analysis is conducted on the classic methods involved in <span id="S4.T7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic Token Merging</span> (Section <a href="#S4.SS1.SSS2" title="4.1.2. Dynamic Token Merging ‣ 4.1. Dynamic Resolution ‣ 4. Dynamic Network ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1.2</span></a>), using ImageNet-1K as the benchmark, with the resolution standardized to <math id="S4.T7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="224\times 224" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>224</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>224</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">224\times 224</annotation></semantics></math>.
The R in “/R” shows the token merging rate.
If <math id="S4.T7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, the model keeps R% of the original tokens. If <math id="S4.T7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, the model is tested after merging tokens into R blocks.
The best-performing method is highlighted in bold, and the runner-up is underlined.

<td id="S4.T7.5.1.14.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right" style="padding-top:1.95pt;padding-bottom:1.95pt;"><span id="S4.T7.5.1.14.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">58</span></td>
<td id="S4.T7.5.1.14.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right" style="padding-top:1.95pt;padding-bottom:1.95pt;"><span id="S4.T7.5.1.14.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">12.2</span></td>
<td id="S4.T7.5.1.14.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right" style="padding-top:1.95pt;padding-bottom:1.95pt;"><span id="S4.T7.5.1.14.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">83.6</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S4.T7.5.1.15" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">
<td id="S4.T7.5.1.15.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:1.95pt;padding-bottom:1.95pt;"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S4.T7.pic29" class="ltx_picture" height="11.07" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 11.07 11.07" width="11.07"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#9962C0;--ltx-fill-color:#9962C0;--ltx-fg-color:#9962C0;" color="#9962C0" fill="#9962C0" stroke="#9962C0" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,11.07) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 11.07 0 L 5.53 11.07 Z"></path></g></svg></span><span id="S4.T7.5.1.15.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;"> TCFormerV2-Base <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib186" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zeng et al., 2022</a>)</cite></span></td>
<td id="S4.T7.5.1.15.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:1.95pt;padding-bottom:1.95pt;"><span id="S4.T7.5.1.15.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">2024</span></td>
<td id="S4.T7.5.1.15.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:1.95pt;padding-bottom:1.95pt;"><span id="S4.T7.5.1.15.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">62.8</span></td>
<td id="S4.T7.5.1.15.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:1.95pt;padding-bottom:1.95pt;"><span id="S4.T7.5.1.15.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">103</span></td>
<td id="S4.T7.5.1.15.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:1.95pt;padding-bottom:1.95pt;"><span id="S4.T7.5.1.15.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">10.8</span></td>
<td id="S4.T7.5.1.15.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:1.95pt;padding-bottom:1.95pt;"><span id="S4.T7.5.1.15.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6E6E6;">83.8</span></td></tr>
</table>
</span></div></div></div>
</figure>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.1.1. </span><span id="S4.SS1.SSS1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic Token Pruning</span></h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In relation to this topic, tokens with insufficient informational content are often directly pruned or sent through a different update path, whereas tokens recognized as having rich semantic information are passed to the deeper layers of the network.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The Top-K pruning method <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib187" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2019</a>)</cite> keeps only the <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> most significant tokens based on their attention weights.
PS-ViT<span id="footnote12" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">12</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">12</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">12</span>
                
                
                
              <a href="https://github.com/yuexy/PS-ViT" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/yuexy/PS-ViT</a></span></span></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib188" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2021</a>)</cite> reduces tokens according to their measured importance to minimize computational costs while retaining performance.
Patch thinning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib90" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tang et al., 2022</a>)</cite> employs a top-down strategy, with later layers guiding the token selection process in earlier layers.
EViT <span id="footnote13" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">13</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">13</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">13</span>
                
                
                
              <a href="https://github.com/youweiliang/evit" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/youweiliang/evit</a></span></span></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib175" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liang et al., 2022</a>)</cite> fuses less important tokens into a single token for further computation, preserving the essence while reducing the number.
Evo-ViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib173" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2021</a>)</cite> is shown in Figure <a href="#S3.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 3.5. Efficient ViT Component Discussion ‣ 3. Efficient ViT Components ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>, regulates the flow of gradient propagation, updating critical tokens slowly and less important ones quickly before merging. IdleViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib179" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2023</a>)</cite> implements a token idling strategy, processing only a subset of tokens in each layer and passing the rest to the next layer unchanged.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Recent studies emphasize the importance of token selection mechanisms adapted to evolving ViT architectures. SPViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib176" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kong et al., 2022</a>)</cite> employs a dynamic multi-head token selector to filter and integrate less informative tokens.
The token compensator (ToCom) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib189" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jie et al., 2024</a>)</cite> proposes a model arithmetic framework to decouple compression degrees between the training and inference stages, addressing performance drops caused by mismatched compression degrees, and achieving universal performance improvements without further training.
HeatViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib177" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dong et al., 2023</a>)</cite> introduces a delay-aware, multi-stage training strategy to optimize token selector performance. TSNet <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib190" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2023</a>)</cite> dynamically selects informative tokens from video samples using a lightweight scoring module, while DynamicViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib94" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rao et al., 2021</a>)</cite> incorporates a learnable module within each transformer block for layer-by-layer token pruning.
TPC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib181" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu, 2024</a>)</cite> uses suspension and reuse probabilities in token selection to preserve computational accuracy. Lastly, the Adaptive Token Sampler (ATS) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib180" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fayyaz et al., 2022</a>)</cite> offers a differentiable parameter-free method for adaptive downsampling, minimizing information loss.
In Figure <a href="#S4.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ 4.1. Dynamic Resolution ‣ 4. Dynamic Network ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>, we present a visual comparison of token pruning strategy methods, generally indicating that the degree of focus on objects demonstrates the ability of the method to identify regions crucial to decision-making.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F11" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2505.03113v3/picture/n7.png" id="S4.F11.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/254;" width="476" height="254" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 11. </span>
<span id="S4.F11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Token Merge Visualization</span>.
Visualize the comparison of token merging methods, where <math id="S4.F11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext='``1/3"' display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>`</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>`</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>"</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">``1/3"</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.F11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext='``2/3"' display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>`</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>`</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>"</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">``2/3"</annotation></semantics></math>, and “All" indicates the stage within the ViT stack structure where the token merging operation is executed. Typically, the shallower layers focus on merging detailed texture information, while the deeper layers attend to the merging of more abstract semantic information.
</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.1.2. </span><span id="S4.SS1.SSS2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic Token Merging</span></h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike pruning methods that discard tokens directly, token merging through strategic token merging, this paradigm can combine less informative tokens with more critical ones, reduce the number of tokens processed, thus contributing to the broader goal of model simplification.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">ToMe <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib184" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bolya et al., 2023</a>)</cite><span id="footnote14" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">14</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">14</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">14</span>
                
                
                
              <a href="https://github.com/facebookresearch/ToMe" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/facebookresearch/ToMe</a> </span></span></span> introduces a fine-tuned matching algorithm to merge similar tokens across layers.
PatchMerger <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib191" title="" class="ltx_ref">Renggli et al., 2022</a>)</cite> allows the network to handle varying token counts by decoupling the number of output tokens from the input, increasing flexibility. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib192" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al., 2023</a>)</cite> presents the token pruning and squeezing (TPS) module, which uses a token merging strategy based on nearest neighbor matching and similarity.
MHSA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib182" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bian et al., 2023</a>)</cite> proposes merging less critical tokens before pruning to maintain crucial information and prevent performance drops. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib193" title="" class="ltx_ref">Feng and Zhang, 2023</a>)</cite> devises a meta-token mechanism to generate an attention map to merge similar tokens. T2T-ViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib194" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yuan et al., 2021</a>)</cite> rearranges the input token sequence to focus on important local structures, facilitating effective token merging. TCFormer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib186" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zeng et al., 2022</a>)</cite> uses progressive clustering to flexibly merge tokens from various locations, capturing detailed information. Lastly, Token Fusion <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib185" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2023</a>)</cite> dynamically combines pruning and merging based on token computation.
Figure <a href="#S4.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ 4.1.1. Dynamic Token Pruning ‣ 4.1. Dynamic Resolution ‣ 4. Dynamic Network ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> presents a visual comparison of token merging strategies, illustrating how merging is performed at varying depths within the ViT architecture.
It is especially noticeable that the initial layers primarily merge fine-grained texture details, whereas the subsequent layers are more focused on integrating higher-level semantic information.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.1.3. </span><span id="S4.SS1.SSS3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Summary: Dynamic Resolution</span></h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Eliminating spatial redundancy enables ViT to offer lightweight online design. By evaluating token importance, it retains, prunes, or merges tokens, ideal for real-time image recognition on high-resolution images or large-scale datasets.
Relevant experimental analyzes are provided in Table  <a href="#S4.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 4.1. Dynamic Resolution ‣ 4. Dynamic Network ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and Table  <a href="#S4.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 4.1. Dynamic Resolution ‣ 4. Dynamic Network ‣ Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, from which it can be observed that:
<span id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">(i).</span> The dynamic resolution strategy can still achieve a lightweight extreme.
For example, Evo-ViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib173" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2021</a>)</cite> has only 5.9M parameters and has a high throughput.
<span id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">(ii).</span> Most methods can significantly improve throughput and reduce FLOPs while slightly decreasing accuracy. For example, DynamicViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib94" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rao et al., 2021</a>)</cite> increases throughput by <math id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="36.6\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>36.6</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">36.6\%</annotation></semantics></math> and reduces FLOPs by <math id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="27.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>27.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> compared to the original DeiT-S model, with only the <math id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> accuracy drop.
<span id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">(iii).</span> Larger models (such as ViT-B, ViT-L) can typically tolerate more aggressive token reduction while maintaining high accuracy. For example, ToMe <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib184" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bolya et al., 2023</a>)</cite> substantially reduces computational cost while maintaining a high accuracy of <math id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>84.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84.2\%</annotation></semantics></math>.
<span id="S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">(iv).</span> Different methods have their own advantages in balancing performance and efficiency. For example, the EViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib195" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liang et al., 2022</a>)</cite> series excels in maintaining high accuracy, while the SuperViT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib183" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lin et al., 2023</a>)</cite> series has more advantages in improving throughput.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2. </span><span id="S4.SS2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Depth Adaptation</span></h3>
